question.problem:
The volume of soda in cans filled at a particular factory is normally distributed with a mean of $12$ ounces and a standard deviation of $0.1$ ounces. What is the probability that a randomly selected soda can contains more than $12.2$ ounces? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.00\,$ | $\,0.01\,$ | $\,0.02\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,2.0\,$ | $\,0.9772\,$ | $\,0.9778\,$ | $\,0.9783\,$ |
| $\,2.1\,$ | $\,0.9821\,$ | $\,0.9826\,$ | $\,0.9830\,$ |
| $\,2.2\,$ | $\,0.9861\,$ | $\,0.9864\,$ | $\,0.9868\,$ |

current_example.problem:
The birth weights of newborns in a given population are normally distributed with a mean of $3\,543$ grams and a standard deviation of $609$ grams. What is the probability that a randomly selected newborn baby weighs more than $3\,100$ grams but less than $3\,600$? Round your answer to $2$ decimal places. *Hint: A table of values of $\Phi(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $\Phi(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *
$z$$\, 0.01 \,$$\, 0.02 \,$$\, 0.03 \,$
$\, -0.8 \,$ $\, 0.2090 \,$ $\, 0.2061 \,$ $\, 0.2033 \,$
$\, -0.7 \,$ $\, 0.2389 \,$ $\, 0.2358 \,$ $\, 0.2327 \,$
$\, -0.6 \,$ $\, 0.2709 \,$ $\, 0.2676 \,$ $\, 0.2643 \,$
$z$$\, 0.08 \,$$\, 0.09 \,$$\, 0.10 \,$
$\, -0.1 \,$ $\, 0.4286 \,$ $\, 0.4247 \,$ $\, 0.4207 \,$
$\, \phantom{-}0.0 \,$ $\, 0.5319 \,$ $\, 0.5359 \,$ $\, 0.5398 \,$
$\, \phantom{-}0.1 \,$ $\, 0.5714 \,$ $\, 0.5753 \,$ $\, 0.5793 \,$
current_example.worked_solution:
Let $X$ represent the weight of a randomly selected baby. Then we have $X \sim N(3\,543, 609^2).$

We want to find $P(3\,100 <   X <  3\,600).$ First, we convert $X$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(3\,100<X<3\,600) & =P(\frac{3\,100-3\,543}{609}<Z<\frac{3\,600-3\,543}{609}) \\  & =P(-0.73<Z<0.09)\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we express the required probability in terms of $\Phi(z)\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.73<Z<0.09) & =P(Z<0.09)-P(Z<-0.73) \\  & =P(Z\le 0.09)-P(Z\le -0.73) \\  & =Φ(0.09)-Φ(-0.73)\end{aligned}
$$

From the table, we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}Φ(-0.73) & =0.2327 \\ Φ(0.09) & =0.5359\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}P(-0.73<Z<0.09) & =Φ(0.09)-Φ(-0.73) \\  & =0.5359-0.2327 \\  & =0.3032.\end{aligned}
$$

In conclusion, the probability that a randomly selected newborn baby weighs more than $3\,100$ grams but less than $3\,600$ is $0.30.$
